candidates: When adding new style properties to a styled component in the Form components that composes multiple style functions (e.g., `styled(X)(styles, sizes, alignment, validation, { newProp })`), verify that the new styles do not unconditionally override earlier prop-driven style functions. A plain object appended at the end of the composition wins over everything before it, so `width: '100%'` appended after `sizes` will silently clobber `size='flex'` (which sets `flex: 1`) and contradict `size='auto'` (which sets `display: 'inline'`). When the new style could conflict with an existing size/variant/prop-driven style, use a function form instead — e.g., `({ size }) => ({ width: !size || size === '100%' ? '100%' : 'auto' })` — so the new property is conditional on the relevant prop.
